2: The polynomial $W(x)$ divided by the binomial $(x-1)$ gives quotient $Q(x)=8x^2+4x-14$ and remainder $R(x)=-5$. Find the roots of the polynomial $W(x)$.
3: The figure shows the graph of the exponential function $f(x)=a^x$ for $x\in\mathbb{R}$, passing through the point $(2,3)$. a) Compute $a$. b) Sketch the graph of the function $g(x)=|f(x)-2|$ and give all values of the parameter $m\in\mathbb{R}$ for which the equation $g(x)=m$ has exactly one solution.
4: There were $k$ coins in the royal treasury. On the morning of the first day the treasurer added 25 coins, and each following morning he added 2 more coins than the previous day. At the same time, each day at noon the king took 50 coins out of the treasury. Compute the smallest number $k$ for which there was at least one coin in the treasury on every day, and then, for that value of $k$, find on which day the treasury held the fewest coins.
7: The sequence $(x-3,\ x+3,\ 6x+2,\ \ldots)$ is an infinite geometric sequence with positive terms. Compute the common ratio of this sequence and justify that $\dfrac{S_{19}}{S_{20}}<\dfrac{1}{4}$, where $S_n$ denotes the sum of the first $n$ terms of this sequence.
10: An urn contains only white and black balls. There are three times as many white balls as black balls. Compute how many balls are in the urn, given that when two balls are drawn simultaneously, the probability of drawing balls of different colors is greater than $\frac{9}{22}$.
11: A regular triangular pyramid is given in which the base edge has length $a$ and the lateral edge is twice as long. Compute the cosine of the angle between a lateral edge and a base edge of the pyramid. Sketch the cross-section of the pyramid by the plane passing through a base edge and the midpoint of the opposite lateral edge, and compute the area of this cross-section.
